notes: EBIT is proxied by GAAP Operating income from the consolidated statements of operations. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001075531/000107553126000009/bkng-20251231.htm))

D&A is proxied by GAAP Depreciation and amortization from the consolidated statements of operations; capex is proxied by cash flow 'Additions to property and equipment'. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001075531/000107553126000009/bkng-20251231.htm))

NWC is defined mechanically as (Total current assets - Total current liabilities) at fiscal year-end; this includes cash and other current items, so it may not equal incremental operating working capital used in operating cash flow modeling. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001075531/000107553126000009/bkng-20251231.htm))

Minority interest was not explicitly identifiable as a separate line item in the 2025 10-K extract used here; set to null. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001075531/000107553126000009/bkng-20251231.htm))
WACC and terminal growth are modeling assumptions for the DCF and were not directly extracted as a single filed point estimate; use sensitivity analysis in the pipeline.

Current price uses the live quote returned by the data lookup; split-adjustment timing may create minor inconsistencies versus historical per-share metrics.

catalysts: Execution of the Transformation Program and reinvestment plan, translating savings into sustained product and marketing performance. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1075531/000107553126000008/q4-25bkngearningsrelease.htm))

Further improvement in operating leverage (EBIT margin) driven by marketing efficiency and technology productivity. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001075531/000107553126000009/bkng-20251231.htm))

Sustained room-night and gross bookings growth in key geographies supporting revenue re-acceleration or margin-defense. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1075531/000107553126000008/q4-25bkngearningsrelease.htm))
company_overview: Booking Holdings operates a multi-brand online travel platform with Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, KAYAK, and OpenTable. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001075531/000107553126000009/bkng-20251231.htm))

Substantially all revenue is generated by online travel reservation services (primarily accommodation), presented on a net basis due to agency/merchant contract structures. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001075531/000107553126000009/bkng-20251231.htm))

Scale, marketing efficiency, and platform technology (including GenAI initiatives) support operating leverage through the cycle. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1075531/000107553126000008/q4-25bkngearningsrelease.htm))
current_context: FY 2025 results: revenue of $26.9B (+13% y/y) with room night growth and expanding profitability metrics. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1075531/000107553126000008/q4-25bkngearningsrelease.htm))

FY 2025 cash generation: net cash provided by operating activities of $9.4B and free cash flow of $9.1B. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1075531/000107553126000008/q4-25bkngearningsrelease.htm))

Management indicated the Transformation Program supports ongoing reinvestment, with savings helping fund strategic technology and growth initiatives in 2026. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1075531/000107553126000008/q4-25bkngearningsrelease.htm))
investment_highlights: Base case starts from GAAP operating income expansion (EBIT margin rising from 2023 to 2025) and assumes modest continued normalization rather than peak-level margins. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001075531/000107553126000009/bkng-20251231.htm))

Revenue growth decelerates each year from 2025’s high-teens pace to mid-single digits by 2030, consistent with a maturing global travel demand cycle. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001075531/000107553126000009/bkng-20251231.htm))

D&A intensity remains stable (modeled near recent ~2.3–2.5% of sales) while capex stays moderate as the platform scales. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001075531/000107553126000009/bkng-20251231.htm))

Working-capital intensity modeled around recent levels (~0.20 of sales), using a consistent balance-sheet definition for NWC. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001075531/000107553126000009/bkng-20251231.htm))
key_risks: Travel demand cyclical downturn or adverse macro conditions reducing bookings velocity and revenue growth. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001075531/000107553126000009/bkng-20251231.htm))

Regulatory/tax developments (including historical tax law impacts) affecting effective tax rate and cash taxes. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001075531/000107553126000009/bkng-20251231.htm))

Competitive pressure in online travel and changing distribution economics (e.g., marketing costs) compressing margins versus the base case. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001075531/000107553126000009/bkng-20251231.htm))

valuation_summary: DCF uses a Gordon-growth terminal framework with a 3% terminal growth rate and an 8% WACC as a conservative starting point for a globally diversified online travel model.

Peer comps show wide dispersion, but forward P/E for selected travel/travel-lodging peers generally lands in a teens-to-30s range, providing sanity-check context for a mature-quality earnings profile. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/expe/statistics/))
